question: Can a defocusing nonlinear Schrödinger equation still blow up?
idea: Defocusing does not prevent every kind of singular behavior in every dimension. The manuscript claims finite-time blowup for an open set of initial data on a twelve-dimensional torus with sufficiently high odd nonlinearity. The blowup persists under the stated Sobolev perturbations; it is not a claim about ordinary three-dimensional regimes.
why: The study of equations that describe how quantities vary across space and time, such as waves, fluids, and heat.
exactClaim: For a sufficiently large odd nonlinearity power, constructs a nonempty open set of initial data in $H^k(\mathbb T^{12})$, with k > 8, whose solutions of the scalar defocusing nonlinear Schrödinger equation blow up in finite time. Thus finite-time blowup is stable under Sobolev perturbations in this supercritical regime. )
reviewStatus: assistant-authored from source summary; not mathematically reviewed
scope: Family-level introduction based on the pinned catalogue summary. Summarizes manuscript claims; not an independent proof review.
